## Summary

TPV Display Technology (Xiamen) is a subsidiary and Xiamen manufacturing base of TPV Technology, which traces its roots to Admiral Overseas Corporation, founded in Taiwan in 1967, owns the AOC, AGON and Envision brands, holds exclusive rights to Philips-branded monitor, TV and AVA businesses worldwide, and runs a dual-track OBM/ODM model, and calls itself one of the world's leading manufacturers of monitors and TVs [2]. Wikipedia describes TPV as headquartered in Kwun Tong, Hong Kong, incorporated in Bermuda, and holding the Philips licence for monitors and entry-level TV sets [3]. The IEEE registry lists four MA-L blocks to this subsidiary at No.1 Xianghai Road in the Xiamen Torch Hi-Tech Industrial Development Zone, three as "TPV Display Technology (Xiamen) Co.,Ltd." and one without the space before the parenthesis [1].

A MAC in these blocks is most likely the network interface of a TV or monitor built by TPV, though no source consulted ties a specific product to these blocks, so device class and found_in are inferred from the group's product line [2][3]. In 2014 ReVuln showed that Philips smart TVs on newer firmware enabled Wi-Fi Miracast by default behind a hard-coded password that could not be changed, so anyone in range could connect, and TP Vision answered that it was working on a fix and recommended switching Wi-Fi Miracast off until a fix arrived [4]; whether TVs built at this Xiamen subsidiary are among those affected is not documented.

No FCC grantee code, radio or silicon record naming this subsidiary was found, and the FCC ID databases refused automated access from this session, so those fields are empty and randomization is unknown.
